PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This notice is provided for construction  use  and maintenance of a new Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) in conjunction with the existing Donald C. Tillman Water Reclamation Plant. The project will include a new approximately 58 743 square foot building. The building consists of four main areas: a basement  first floor  second floor  and outdoor chemical storage and pumping.  The building is 43.4 feet in height at its highest point. The first floor will include building operations  treatment system  laboratory (calibration room)  meeting room  break room  electrical room  mechanical room and miscellaneous support spaces on the first floor. The second floor will house a visitor’s center (educational and display area for school tours) that pertains to the processes occurring in the building.  The basement consists of a mechanical room  electrical room and piping corridor.  The chemical feed and storage area is an outdoor area covered by a canopy.  Outside of the building there will be four pumping stations serving the treatment system.  The pump stations consist of the MF Feed Pump Station  MF Backwash Pump Station  RO Feed Pump Station and RO Backwash Pump Station.  The MF Feed Pump Station and MF Backwash Pump Station are separate structures located in an area to the west of the new building; the RO pumping stations are exterior but connected to the building. There will be several underground utilities serving the new building and pumping stations.  These underground utilities consist of piping between the pumping stations and the building  piping connecting the treatment system to the existing Balboa Pump Station  piping connecting the treatment system to sewers within the DC Tillman Treatment Facility  potable water connecting to the building for lavatories and the breakroom and for the fire sprinkler system.  Electrical service to the building will be constructed underground.  The exterior of the building will have a drop-off area for visitors and two gathering areas for visitors.  These areas will be landscaped.  No existing structure will be demolished under this project. The new building will operate 24 hours per day  7 days per week  while the educational center will be open to the public by appointment Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The new Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) will be constructed at the southeast corner of DC Tillman Water Reclamation Facility (DCTWRP) site. The new facility is located adjacent to a public park on the south  cricket field on the east  and DCTWRTP on the west and north sides.  I-405 Freeway is located 2040 lf to the east and Woodley Avenue is located 1940 lf to the west of the new AWPF.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This Form 7460 is being filed per an existing "Grant of Avigation and Noise Easement." Attached is an abbreviated copy of the easement document  page 3 contains the requirement for filing of Form 7460. The project does not contain a transmitting station  antenna or microwave facilities. The project will utilize underground electrical  telephone & data utilities.  There are no existing buildings or other structures on the project site.nnThe proposed building is a warehouse & distribution facility with related infrastructure.  The building is approximately 42 000 square foot ("s.f.")  30 000 s.f. for the primary area & 12 000 s.f. for the exterior canopy where vehicles will be loaded. The warehouse will likely be a pre-engineered metal building. Attached are preliminary building plans.nnThe proposed distribution facility will operate 24/7 to support the delivery of packages to customer locations between 9:00 AM & 2:00 PM. The facility will receive shipments that are sorted based on zip codes & dispatched for delivery to customers. It is anticipated that line haul trucks will deliver packages to the facility each day.  Most of the sortation is done in the middle of the night & then the items are transferred to a van or to a flex driver. There will be approximately 62 on-site employees & 25 van drivers to support this operation. In addition  there will be up to 82 flex drivers that will use personal vehicles to deliver packages & work in concert with standard van drivers.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: This notice is provided for construction  use  and maintenance of a new Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) in conjunction with the existing Donald C. Tillman Water Reclamation Plant. The project will include a new approximately 58 743 square foot building. The building consists of four main areas: a basement  first floor  second floor  and outdoor chemical storage and pumping.  The building is 43.4 feet in height at its highest point. The first floor will include building operations  treatment system  laboratory (calibration room)  meeting room  break room  electrical room  mechanical room and miscellaneous support spaces on the first floor. The second floor will house a visitor’s center (educational and display area for school tours) that pertains to the processes occurring in the building.  The basement consists of a mechanical room  electrical room and piping corridor.  The chemical feed and storage area is an outdoor area covered by a canopy.  Outside of the building there will be four pumping stations serving the treatment system.  The pump stations consist of the MF Feed Pump Station  MF Backwash Pump Station  RO Feed Pump Station and RO Backwash Pump Station.  The MF Feed Pump Station and MF Backwash Pump Station are separate structures located in an area to the west of the new building; the RO pumping stations are exterior but connected to the building. There will be several underground utilities serving the new building and pumping stations.  These underground utilities consist of piping between the pumping stations and the building  piping connecting the treatment system to the existing Balboa Pump Station  piping connecting the treatment system to sewers within the DC Tillman Treatment Facility  potable water connecting to the building for lavatories and the breakroom and for the fire sprinkler system.  Electrical service to the building will be constructed underground.  The exterior of the building will have a drop-off area for visitors and two gathering areas for visitors.  These areas will be landscaped.  No existing structure will be demolished under this project. The new building will operate 24 hours per day  7 days per week  while the educational center will be open to the public by appointment Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The new Advanced Water Purification Facility (AWPF) will be constructed at the southeast corner of DC Tillman Water Reclamation Facility (DCTWRP) site. The new facility is located adjacent to a public park on the south  cricket field on the east  and DCTWRTP on the west and north sides.  I-405 Freeway is located 2040 lf to the east and Woodley Avenue is located 1940 lf to the west of the new AWPF.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The intent of this project to improve traffic operations from Harry Reid International Airport along Tropicana Avenue and University Center Drive (UCD)  with particular attention to improving two major intersections: Tropicana/UCD and Tropicana/Paradise. Tropicana Avenue is a major arterial roadway (the 2018 traffic volume on Tropicana west of Paradise road was 101 000 ADT) with pedestrian sidewalks on both sides originally constructed in the 1950's and borders the Airport to the north. A major University and heavily developed areas are located north of Tropicana Avenue  therefore relocating the road completely outside of the existing Harry Reid International Airport Runway Protection Zone (RPZ) is not possible. Traffic volumes at both major intersections along Tropicana Avenue are projected to exponentially increase by year 2040 (travel times will increase 43% on average) thereby substantially increasing travel times to and from the Airport  lengthening vehicular traffic static time within the RPZ  increasing the probability for vehicular accidents  and increasing emergency responder travel time to this area.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: Tropicana Avenue and University Center Drive Grade Separation project is located in the general vicinity of in the vicinity of Harry Reid International Airport that will improve access to and from the Resort Corridor. The limits of the grade separation extend to Wilbur Street to the east and Naples Channel alignment to the west. This project consists of a realignment of Tropicana Avenue within the above-mentioned limits to the north and undercrossings at Paradise Road and University Center Drive. Westbound Tropicana will be depressed within this area for the most part. Eastbound Tropicana remains at grade and crosses over westbound in two locations. Through traffic within westbound Tropicana Avenue will travel uninterruptedly between Wilbur Street and Koval Lane. A portion of this project is located within Reid Airport Runway Protection Zone (RPZ).

This project consists of a realignment of Tropicana Avenue within the above-mentioned limits to the north and undercrossings at Paradise Road and University Center Drive. Westbound Tropicana will be depressed within this area for the most part. Eastbound Tropicana remains at grade and crosses over westbound in two locations. Through traffic within westbound Tropicana Avenue will travel uninterruptedly between Wilbur Street and Koval Lane. A portion of this project is located within Reid Airport Runway Protection Zone (RPZ).

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: The intent of this project to improve traffic operations from Harry Reid International Airport along Tropicana Avenue and University Center Drive (UCD)  with particular attention to improving two major intersections: Tropicana/UCD and Tropicana/Paradise. Tropicana Avenue is a major arterial roadway (the 2018 traffic volume on Tropicana west of Paradise road was 101 000 ADT) with pedestrian sidewalks on both sides originally constructed in the 1950's and borders the Airport to the north. A major University and heavily developed areas are located north of Tropicana Avenue  therefore relocating the road completely outside of the existing Harry Reid International Airport Runway Protection Zone (RPZ) is not possible. Traffic volumes at both major intersections along Tropicana Avenue are projected to exponentially increase by year 2040 (travel times will increase 43% on average) thereby substantially increasing travel times to and from the Airport  lengthening vehicular traffic static time within the RPZ  increasing the probability for vehicular accidents  and increasing emergency responder travel time to this area.
